scope: User-authorised project/repository rename, supplied artwork replacement, current documentation/install references and provenance reconciliation. This record does not authorise changes to household device configuration or assert a fresh live Home Assistant acceptance run.

current_identity.household_identity: Optional family name, crest or business logo; project identity is not mandatory within Home Assistant.

historical_context.boundary: These names identify earlier records, not current installation destinations. Prior review JSON, original evidence, dated page history and original illustration creator credits remain unchanged. GitHub repository redirects do not imply that the former Pages URL redirects.

authority.decision: The user explicitly requested the new project/repository name and deletion/replacement of old logos. Earlier local instructions to preserve V3.2 supplied identity do not override that request. Official GOV.UK marks remain prohibited.

supplied_artwork.handling: Original source archive metadata remains byte-identical. The accepted manifest records omitted empty WebP and supplied count/self-hash defects explicitly. Superseded logo files are removed from current source; earlier identity remains available through Git history. Original explanatory illustration geometry and creator credits are preserved.

compatibility: The bare civica default is added alongside twenty named palette themes; the legacy govuk alias and YAML remain.
The canonical card asset is civica-house-lighting-card.js; the old resource filename is an import shim and the old custom element remains registered.
Existing lighting automation and entity identifiers are preserved; no physical configuration migration is inferred from a branding request.
Companion artwork URLs include package version 1.4.0 to avoid reusing cached superseded logos after an upgrade.
The installer documents replacing the owned supplied-brand directory after backup, avoiding a merge that leaves superseded logos installed.

primary_source_review.finding: Repository information and Git operations redirect after a rename. Project Pages URLs do not. Update the remote and current documentation links; do not reuse the former repository name if its redirects are required.
The listed repository catalogue handles a renamed repository. This does not by itself verify every existing custom-repository installation.
Custom repositories use the GitHub API. Metadata refresh and installation/file changes are distinct operations.
Update information refreshes metadata; Redownload updates installed files. Remove deletes installed repository files, so remove/re-add is not the default rename instruction.

Reviewed current upstream source detects a changed repository full name, records the rename and retries the update. This source evidence supports refreshing the existing entry first; it is not a claim about the installed HACS version.

The reviewed theme repository handler derives the local directory from the YAML filename. Retaining the compatibility YAML avoids treating a repository rename as authority to change installed theme ownership.

findings_resolved: Updated the dynamic original-evidence GitHub template to the current repository while preserving captured revisions and paths.
Replaced the current audit note that incorrectly treated V3.2 artwork as authoritative after the user supplied its replacement.
Preserved dated page history and historical workflow/source receipts, with exact bounded naming exceptions instead of a blind zero-match claim.
Confirmed the chart colour engine diff changes only its creator-name comment; refreshed the example generator SHA without changing the colour algorithm or assertions.
Relocated eighteen current evidence lines to their unchanged exact excerpts after frontmatter and stylesheet additions.
The naming guard distinguishes official GOV.UK source titles and legacy compatibility tokens from retired project names.
independent_review.method: Owner-frozen source inspection, exact evidence matching, unchanged-history hashes, a bounded current-name scan and targeted guard regressions. Earlier runtime/visual passes are not reclassified as fresh rebrand acceptance.

limitations: Text checks do not prove logo geometry, raster correctness or a successful remote migration; asset byte checks, rendered examples and public verification remain separate.
